verdict: NO COURT WAS HELD - refutability scored 4/10 and the runner routed it straight to ADJUDICATE by design. The triage record is unusually strong for a 4/10 and its central finding is that DGXX never belonged on this docket in the form the screen produced it. DGXX is not a Finance name: it is Digi Power X (formerly Digihost), a bitcoin miner converting to AI colocation and GPU-as-a-service, so the 'excess vs Finance sector median -0.504' that generated the event row is a TAGGING ARTIFACT, not dispersion. Against the correct cohort - BTC miners pivoting to AI/HPC - a -57.5% drawdown is roughly cohort-typical. The triage classes it STRUCTURAL against the equity-funded-buildout narrative, and the mechanism is identified and confirmed rather than suspected: shares outstanding went 36.5M (6/30/25) to 62.5M (12/31/25) to 70M (3/31/26) to about 90.4M now, which is +65.3% YoY and roughly +30% in the June quarter alone; $72.36M of the initial $75M ATM tranche was already sold as of 5/8/26 and the program was upsized to $175M at a 3.0% commission; and the CFO stated on 7/3/26 that the $155M of cash is 'entirely from our own resources', i.e. zero project-level debt has closed. Dilution is the funding model, not an accident. The triage's pre-print reconstruction is the decisive work: the loudest bull claim (about $155M cash, zero long-term debt, self-funded, FY27 run-rate $250-300M) is a financing artifact. Bridging $57.8M of cash at 3/31, less roughly $50M of June-quarter Alabama capex, less opex and working capital, plus about $15M of digital assets if monetized, to the $155M at 7/3 implies roughly $135-145M of equity issued in Q2 - which matches the ~20M share increase and, importantly, EXCEEDS the ~$102.6M of ATM headroom remaining at 5/8/26. Either a further upsize, a marketed deal, or larger digital-asset sales closed the gap, and public text cannot distinguish them. The remaining funding gap is the same story forward: about $95M spent to date against a further ~$150M+ to complete 40MW, fundable only by continuing to sell stock unless the 'project-level financing underway' (explicitly not yet documented) closes. The one leg that is genuinely damage-absent is counterparty credit, and the triage killed it as a bear leg honestly: the $1.1B/10yr MSA counterparty is Cerebras Systems, which IPO'd 2026-05-14 raising $5.55B on $510M of 2025 revenue and $237.8M of net income. So 'fake or insolvent counterparty' is dead, but that was never the leg driving the discount - 'you get diluted before Dec-2026 revenue' is, and it is confirmed. What makes this a clean park rather than a court is the asymmetry of what is knowable: Q2 revenue falling QoQ on the legacy mining wind-down with a widening loss is already knowable and therefore should not be traded, while the only genuine pop scenarios - a signed non-dilutive project financing, a Cerebras prepayment or deposit, or a hard reaffirmation of the Dec-15-2026 Phase 1 in-service date - cannot be handicapped. And with a live ATM the company sells into exactly that pop, capping the upside you would be buying. Under the response taxonomy this is a structural business-risk kill with a capped-upside timing objection layered on top.
